title: recipe: what is template data set?
description:
Hello everyone,

A huge thank you for the quality of this package. I am just a beginner in ML and, thanks to you, I am able to perform analyses that I thought were beyond my reach! Thank you!

However, I have a question regarding the `recipe()` function. It is stated in the help that the `x=` argument of this function is a _template data set_. What does this exactly mean? In most of the online examples available, it is the training sample, but what should I do in a case like mine (see below)? Can I use the original database as a _template_? Does this choice have an impact on the validity of my workflow?

I know that my code is not entirely reproducible, but the data is confidential, I apologize for that.

Best regards

```r
# Original DB
db.glmnet

set.seed(123)

# Create 100 instances for group-wise Monte Carlo cross-validation
train <- group_mc_cv(
  # Specify the data frame containing the data
  db.glmnet,
  # Specify the number of times to repeat the cross-validation
  times = 100,
  # Specify the proportion of data to be used for training in each split
  prop = 1/2,
  # Specify the grouping variable to ensure that all instances from the same group are in the same split
  group = XXX
)
# Reverse the splits to create the test set
test <- reverse_splits(
  # Specify the training splits object created earlier
  train
)

# Define the recipe for preprocessing with normalization
preprocess <- recipe(
  # Specify the formula for the recipe
  DV ~ FEATURE01 + FEATURE02 + FEATURE03 + FEATURE04 + FEATURE05 + FEATURE06 + FEATURE07 + FEATURE08 + FEATURE09,
  # Specify the data to be used in the recipe
  data = db.glmnet) %>%
  # Remove variables with zero variance
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  # Center and scale (i.e., normalize) all the predictors
  step_normalize(all_predictors()
)

# Specify the Lasso regression model for classification
lasso <-
  # Use the multinom_reg function to specify a multinomial logistic regression model
  multinom_reg(
    # The penalty parameter is set to tune(), which means it will be tuned during the model training process
    penalty = tune(),
    # The mixture parameter is set to 1, indicating that a LASSO model
    mixture = 1
  ) %>%
  # Set the mode of the model to classification
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  # Set the engine to glmnet
  set_engine("glmnet", maxit = 10^7)
  # The maxit parameter is set to 10^7, which specifies the maximum number of iterations for the optimization algorithm

# Create a workflow object
wf <-
  # Initialize a new workflow
  workflow() %>%
  # Add the preprocessing recipe to the workflow
  add_recipe(preprocess) %>%
  # Add the Lasso regression model to the workflow
  add_model(lasso)
  
# Search Grid to find an optimal Lambda value
grid <- grid_regular(
  # Specify the range for the penalty parameter (Lambda)
  penalty(range = c(-4, 0)),
  # Specify the number of levels in the grid
  levels = 100
)

# Set the parallel plan to use all available CPU cores for parallel processing
plan(multisession, workers = 4)

# Perform hyperparameter tuning using a grid search
tuning <- wf %>% # Specify the workflow object that includes the preprocessing recipe and the model
    tune_grid(
    # Specify the resampling scheme (cross-validation splits) created earlier
    resamples = train,
    # Specify the grid of hyperparameter values to search over
    grid = grid,
    # Specify the control parameters for the tuning process
    control = control_grid(
      # Set verbose to FALSE to suppress detailed output during tuning
      verbose = FALSE,
      # Set save_workflow to TRUE to save the workflow objects for each hyperparameter combination
      save_workflow = TRUE,
      # Set save_pred to TRUE to save the predictions for each hyperparameter combination
      save_pred = TRUE
    ),
    # Specify the metrics to evaluate the model performance
    metrics = metric_set(bal_accuracy, mn_log_loss, roc_auc)
  )

# Set the plan to sequential execution for subsequent operations
plan(sequential)
```

title: Last_fit() and fit()
description:
I am creating this issue because I do not know how to obtain the same regression metrics with last_fit() and fit(). Please see below an example:

```r
library(tidymodels)
set.seed(123)
data_split <- initial_split(mtcars, prop = 0.8)
train_data <- training(data_split)
test_data  <- testing(data_split)
rf_recipe <- 
  recipe(mpg ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
rf_spec <- 
  rand_forest(
    mtry = tune(),
    trees = tune()
  ) %>%
  set_engine("ranger") %>%
  set_mode("regression")
set.seed(234)
car_folds <- vfold_cv(train_data, v = 5)
rf_workflow <- 
  workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(rf_recipe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)
rf_grid <- grid_regular(
  mtry(range = c(1, 6)),
  trees(range = c(100, 500)),
  levels = 4
)
rf_tuned <- tune_grid(
  rf_workflow,
  resamples = car_folds,
  grid = rf_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse)
)
best_rf <- select_best(rf_tuned, metric = "rmse")
final_rf <- finalize_workflow(rf_workflow, best_rf)
rf_final_fit <- last_fit(final_rf, split = data_split)
rf_final_fit %>% collect_metrics()
```

Here I get an rsme of 2.14. But with fit():

```r
 fit_res <- fit(final_rf, data = train_data)
augment(fit_res, new_data = test_data) %>%
rmse(truth = mpg, estimate = .pred)
```

I get 2.25. Is it possible anyhow both results to match?

title: tidymodels_prefer activates `conflicted` machinery without attaching `conflicted`
description:
After running `tidymodels_prefer`, `conflicted`'s machinery gets activated, so we get errors on *other* conflicts that have not yet been declared. The main `dplyr` conflicts are already handled, but there are conflicts in other packages that trigger the warning.

The main problem is that someone trying to handle the `conflicted` error correctly gets a command that won't run without `library(conflicted)`.

Example:

``` r
library(mosaic)
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'mosaic':
#>   method                           from   
#>   fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame ggplot2
#> 
#> The 'mosaic' package masks several functions from core packages in order to add 
#> additional features.  The original behavior of these functions should not be affected by this.
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'mosaic'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:dplyr':
#> 
#>     count, do, tally
#> The following object is masked from 'package:Matrix':
#> 
#>     mean
# ... more similar messages

library(tidymodels)
tidymodels_prefer()
mean(c(5, 1))
#> Error:
#> ! [conflicted] `mean` found in 3 packages.
#> Either pick the one you want with `::` 
#> * mosaic::mean
#> * Matrix::mean
#> * base::mean
#> Or declare a preference with `conflict_prefer()`
#> * conflict_prefer("mean", "mosaic")
#> * conflict_prefer("mean", "Matrix")
#> * conflict_prefer("mean", "base")
conflict_prefer("mean", "base") # ok let's try to follow that advice
#> Error in conflict_prefer("mean", "base"): could not find function "conflict_prefer"
```

<sup>Created on 2022-05-27 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Possible solution might be to have `tidymodels_prefer` attach `conflicted`.

title: Prediction fails when all variables are normalized
description:
## The problem

I've been exploring `tidymodels` and I encountered a problem where `predict()` fails especially when "ALL" of variables are normalized, which includes dependant variable. I do not observe same error when only predictor variables are normalized.

split = initial_split(data, prop = 0.75)

test = testing(split)

  recipe(Sepal.Width ~ Petal.Length, data = train

  step_normalize(everything())

  recipe(Sepal.Width ~ Petal.Length, data = train
  ) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_predictors())

model = linear_reg() %>% 
  set_engine('lm')

workflow_all = workflow() %>% 
  add_model(model) %>% 
  add_recipe(all_recipe)

workflow_x = workflow() %>% 
  add_model(model) %>% 
  add_recipe(x_recipe)

title: Issue when  trying to fine tune a random forest regression model using spatialsample as a resampling strategy
description:
Very new to `tidymodels` so bear with me. Following this [example](https://juliasilge.com/blog/ikea-prices/), I want to perform a random forest regression. The difference is that because I have spatial data (points) I am using the `spatialsample` package for resampling. All works well using the default parameters for the random forest (RF) model. So, when I do:

```
recipe <- recipes::recipe(eq1, data = sf::st_drop_geometry(ames_sf))

# modeling
ranger_spec <-
  rand_forest() %>% 
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine("ranger")

ranger_workflow <- 
  workflow(recipe, ranger_spec) |> 
  tune::fit_resamples(folds)
```

everything's okay.

But when I try to fine tune the model parameters, like so:

```
recipe <- recipes::recipe(eq1, data = sf::st_drop_geometry(ames_sf))

# modeling
ranger_spec <-
  rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 501) %>% # in this line is the difference with the above code
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine("ranger")

ranger_workflow <- 
  workflow(recipe, ranger_spec) |> 
  tune::fit_resamples(folds)
```

I'm getting this error:

```
Error:
! 2 arguments have been tagged for tuning in these components: model_spec. 
Please use one of the tuning functions (e.g. `tune_grid()`) to optimize them.
```

Moreover, I tried something like this:

```
recipe <- recipes::recipe(eq1, data = sf::st_drop_geometry(ames_sf))

# modeling

  rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 501) %>% 
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine("ranger")

ranger_workflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(recipe) %>%
  add_model(ranger_spec)

set.seed(678)
doParallel::registerDoParallel()
ranger_tune <-
  tune_grid(ranger_workflow,
            tune::fit_resamples(folds), # or resamples =  tune::fit_resamples(folds)
            grid = 5 
)
```

I am getting this error:

```
Error in `tune::fit_resamples()`:
! The first argument to [fit_resamples()] should be either a model or workflow.

But, if I type:

```
ranger_tune <-
  tune_grid(ranger_workflow,

It works but I am not sure if that's the right way.

Could you please help me on how could I tune the hyperparameters of the RF model using spatial resampling strategy?

title: Possible xgboost bug
description:
Hi,

I'm working on the integration of tidymodels with DALEX. My goal is to allow the user to achieve an explanation using the original dataframe as well as the adjusted dataframe (after all workflow transformations). However I've encountered a problem related with xgboost and I kindly ask for a solution, because perhaps I don't understand some things. Here is an example (courtesy of @Sponghop). Let's start with randomForest model.

```
### MODEL TRAINING PART ###

data(PimaIndiansDiabetes)
set.seed(1234)
pid_split <- initial_split(PimaIndiansDiabetes, prop = .75)
pid_train <- training(pid_split)
pid_test <- testing(pid_split)

mod_rec <-
  recipe(diabetes ~ ., data = pid_train) %>%
  step_mutate(was_pregnant = as.factor(ifelse(pregnant > 0, 'Ja', 'Nee'))) %>%
  step_dummy(was_pregnant) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric())

randomforest_mod <-
  rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("randomForest") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

ml_wflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(mod_rec) %>%
  add_model(randomforest_mod)

ctrl <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)
folds <- vfold_cv(pid_train, v = 2, repeats = 3)
grid <-  expand.grid(mtry = 1:6, trees = c(250,500,750))

all_cores <- parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE) - 1
registerDoFuture()
cl <- makeCluster(all_cores)
plan(future::cluster, workers = cl)

res <- 
  ml_wflow %>%
  tune_grid(resamples = folds, control = ctrl, grid = grid)

stopCluster(cl)

res %>%
  tune::collect_metrics()

best_params <-
  res %>%
  tune::select_best(metric = "accuracy")
best_params

reg_res_randomforest <-
  ml_wflow %>%
  # Attach the best tuning parameters to the model
  finalize_workflow(best_params) %>%
  # Fit the final model to the training data
  fit(data = pid_train)


### END OF MODEL TRAINING ###
```

As far as I understand, now I can achieve proper prediction in two ways

```
### 1ST WAY

predict(reg_res_randomforest, pid_train, type = "prob")

### 2ND WAY

data  <- as.data.frame(prep(reg_res_randomforest$pre$actions$recipe$recipe, pid_train) %>% bake(pid_train))
predict(reg_res_randomforest$fit$fit, data, type = "prob")
```

Works just fine. However, for xgboost models it does not work as smoothly. 

```
### MODEL TRAINING PART ###

data(PimaIndiansDiabetes)
set.seed(1234)
pid_split <- initial_split(PimaIndiansDiabetes, prop = .75)
pid_train <- training(pid_split)
pid_test <- testing(pid_split)

mod_rec <-
  recipe(diabetes ~ ., data = pid_train) %>%
  step_mutate(was_pregnant = as.factor(ifelse(pregnant > 0, 'Ja', 'Nee'))) %>%
  step_dummy(was_pregnant) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric())

xgboost_mod <-
  boost_tree(mtry = tune(), tree_depth = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

ml_wflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(mod_rec) %>%
  add_model(xgboost_mod)

ctrl <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)
folds <- vfold_cv(pid_train, v = 2, repeats = 3)
grid <-  expand.grid(mtry = 3:11, tree_depth = 3:11)

all_cores <- parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE) - 1
registerDoFuture()
cl <- makeCluster(all_cores)
plan(future::cluster, workers = cl)

res <- 
  ml_wflow %>%
  tune_grid(resamples = folds, control = ctrl, grid = grid)

stopCluster(cl)

res %>%
  tune::collect_metrics()

best_params <-
  res %>%
  tune::select_best(metric = "accuracy")
best_params


reg_res_xgboost <-
  ml_wflow %>%
  finalize_workflow(best_params) %>%
  fit(data = pid_train)

pid_test <- testing(pid_split)

reg_res_xgboost %>%
  predict(new_data = pid_test) %>%
  bind_cols(pid_test, .) %>%
  select(diabetes, .pred_class) %>% 
  accuracy(diabetes, .pred_class)


### END OF MODEL TRAINING ###

1ST WAY

predict(reg_res_xgboost, pid_train, type = "prob")

### 2ND WAY

data  <- as.data.frame(prep(reg_res_xgboost$pre$actions$recipe$recipe, pid_train) %>% bake(pid_train))
predict(reg_res_xgboost$fit$fit, data, type = "prob")
```

and 2nd way fails with an error

```
Error in 'xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(data = newdata, missing = NA)':
  'data' has class 'character' and length 5760.
  'data' accepts either a numeric matrix or a single filename.
```

I suspect the problem is probably related to matrix evaluation for the raw xgboost model. My question however is whether that behavior is intended or not. I assume that reg_res_xgboost$fit$fit is a regular parsnip model (am I right?), thus it should work after preprocessing the data according to workflow even if newdata is a data.frame and not a matrix, but perhaps I'm mistaken.

Best regards
Szymon Maksymiuk

title: Decision tree problem with factor conversion
description:

I'm afraid I was beaten with a simple classification decision tree use case and I kindly ask for help.

I want to perform classification task on `titanic_imputed` dataset from `DALEX` package. Thing is, target variable which is `survived` is numeric in this dataset, therefore in order to conduct classification I have to convert it into a factor. I want to use a recipe for that purpose. First try:

```

library("tidymodels")
library("recipes")
rec <- recipe(survived ~ ., data = titanic_imputed) %>%
       step_mutate(survived = as.factor(survived)) %>%
       prep()
model <- decision_tree(tree_depth = 25) %>%
         set_engine("rpart") %>%
         set_mode("classification")

wflow <- workflow() %>%
         add_recipe(rec) %>%
         add_model(model)


model_fitted <- wflow %>%
                fit(data = titanic_imputed)

predict(model_fitted, titanic_imputed)
```

Unfortunately predict function returns an error (may be slightly different, I translated it from my locale)

x object 'survived' wasn't found
